env_override.note: an integer string, the shape a workflow sets
set but empty — a shell expanding an unset var
a unit suffix, which float() will not take
zero is not 'no ceiling', it is a typo

invariant_override.note: raising the FAST ceiling must not move invariant's: one variable per suite (ADR-017, PR #29 R15)
invariant has its own variable, so CI can measure its own number the way `fast` already does

expect.note: six things: `over_budget` says 75.00s is inside the fast ceiling and 75.01s is not, and the same at 15.00/15.01 for invariant; WALL_BUDGET_S holds exactly {fast, invariant}, checked as a set; EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S moves the FAST ceiling for a positive number, falls back to the committed 75 for everything else, and never touches invariant's; `evals.run.main()` returns 1 on an over-budget total and 0 otherwise; and .github/workflows/eval.yml declares the CI ceiling this case pins

provenance: the `fast` gate's wall clock went 13s (M2) -> 48.6s (M6) -> 55.4s (M7) -> 67.5s (M8) without one run ever turning red, because ADR-002 Decision 4's 60s ceiling was prose in an ADR and nothing read it. This case has been falsified three times, each one level up from the last, and carries a half for each. (1) It first read `sorted(evals/report/*-fast.json)[-1]`; on the fresh clone `.github/workflows/eval.yml` builds, the newest file is always the report the branch committed, so a tree measuring 77.23s still scored 89/89 = 1.000 with the gate green (PR #20 R1). (2) It then graded `evals.run.over_budget` alone, and the five-line block in `main()` that applies it was pinned by nothing: deleting `evals/run.py`'s `if over_budget(args.suite, totals["wall_seconds"]):` left a 79.02s run — 32% over — reporting 90/90 = 1.000 at exit 0 with this case PASSing (PR #20 R8). Watched red with that block deleted and nothing else touched: `[FAIL] fast-wall-clock-budget`, 89/90 = 0.989 against baseline 1.000, wrong: [{wall_seconds: 79.02, exit: 1, got: 0}] — failing on the run that should have been stopped and not on the one that should not. (3) The ceiling then met CI for the first time and turned out never to have run there: main's own CI does `fast` in 89.62s, ~50% over the same 60s, invisibly. The ceiling became per-environment (ADR-013 Decision 3), so the override is now part of the ruling. Both directions watched red before it existed: with `wall_budget` ignoring the environment, the two positive-value rows fail (`{'env': '95', 'expected_ceiling': 95.0, 'got': 60}`); with an unguarded `float()` that lets garbage mean 'no ceiling', six rows fail (`{'env': None, 'expected_ceiling': 60, 'got': inf}`). The workflow row was red before `.github/workflows/eval.yml` declared anything: `{'workflow': 'EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S', 'declared': None, 'expected': 75}`. (4) And then CI falsified the case one more way, on the run that was supposed to confirm it: it passed locally and failed on CI with `{'suite': 'fast', 'wall_seconds': 70.01, 'over': true}`, because `over_budget` reads the ambient environment and the workflow exports EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S=75 — so 70.01s was correctly not over budget there, and the row asserting otherwise was simply wrong. A case about environment-dependent ceilings that was itself environment-dependent. The rows and the `main()` probes now run with the override cleared, and the fix reproduces both ways: `EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S=75` green, unset green. (5) Round 4 review found the ceiling amendment (60->70) itself was avoidable: `readyz-tracks-the-run-slot`'s `hold_seconds: 3.0` graded the idle->busy->idle transition, not the duration, and ADR-013 Decision 4's claim that 'the sweep above found no third [waste shape]' was false — this was a third one, still in the suite (PR #20 R14). Reduced to `hold_seconds: 2.0` from a margin argument on the actual start-race (submission-to-busy measured at 4.3-5.2ms typically, one 62ms outlier; 2.0s leaves a 0.67s sample gap, ~10x the worst outlier), not copied from the value review happened to measure passing. Recovered ~1.0s per suite run, but a post-fix seven-run band (58.69-60.59s) was published as still straddling 60 on two of seven, so branch 1 (revert to 60) was declared unavailable even after the fix; the published band's slowest run (60.59) fed the same +15%-round-up-to-5 rule to 70s (R15), and `WALL_BUDGET_S` moved to 70. (6) Round 5 review could not reproduce that band: 8 reviewer runs (59.00-59.87) and 6 orchestrator runs at load average 3.19 (58.97-59.22), plus the orchestrator's own committed gate run (59.15) — ~15 runs, none over 60, against the published 60.44 and 60.59. Asked to substantiate the two outliers as loaded-machine runs before dropping them, the repair ran 7 more: 6 at load average 2.3-4.9 (58.97-59.41) and one deliberately under artificial load — 8 CPU-pinned `yes` processes, load average driven to 8.4 on a 14-core machine — which measured 58.96s, at the low end rather than the high end of the range. Heavy concurrent CPU load did not reproduce a slowdown, let alone push the suite over 60s: this suite's wall clock is dominated by fixed sleeps and timeout bounds, not CPU contention, so 'busy machine' does not explain the two outliers and they are dropped as unsubstantiated. Across three independent measurers, ~22 runs, idle and deliberately loaded alike, land at 58.96-59.87s; a published band presented as an unconditioned measurement had two runs nobody else — including a dedicated attempt to reproduce them under load — could reproduce. `WALL_BUDGET_S` reverted to 60 on that evidence. (7) The revert commit's own claim — headroom ~0.13s against a max reproducible run of 59.87 — did not survive its own verification: 21 further real (non-stubbed) runs against the reverted, committed tree found the honest band is 58.83-60.26s, and the very first of those 21 landed at 60.26s, over the just-reverted ceiling, at ordinary load with no concurrent stress. 20 of the next 21 stayed under 60. Combined with the earlier 22, three independent measurers now have 43 non-original-band runs against this tree: 42 under 60, 1 over, by 0.26s. `WALL_BUDGET_S` stays 60 on that weight of evidence (roughly 95-98% of runs, honestly counted, clear it, against the withdrawn band's claimed 71%), but the record states the residual openly rather than the falsely precise '~0.13s of headroom' the first revert shipped with — a claim that was itself falsified within the same review round it was written in, the same pattern this repo has recorded before: a declared limitation or guarantee gets demonstrated wrong within days, sometimes within the same sitting, and the fix is to say what is actually reproducible, not to round it to a cleaner number. (8) PR #29 R13: the ceiling finally became a coin flip on a commit that changed nothing but JSON — 60.24s against 60, 109/109 passing. M31 had added real cost and the first repair moved three browser cases to `invariant`-only tags instead of facing it, which took ~4.9s out of the measured number and left the gate non-deterministic while the published `fast` figure stayed at 59.7s. ADR-017 amends Decision 4: the three cases are back in `fast`, the local ceiling is re-measured to 75 by this ADR's own rule (slowest observed +15%, rounded up to a multiple of five), and `invariant` gets a ceiling of its own at 15 so a tag can never again be an unbounded relief valve. This case grades both suites now, despite its id — the `suites_with_a_ceiling` set check is what makes a third suite appearing without a number turn it red, and the new `invariant_override` rows pin that CI's EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S=80 does not raise invariant's.

triage.note: grades a rule and the place it is applied, because holes have appeared at both. `_main_exit_code` drives the real `evals.run.main()` with `load_cases`/`run_case` stubbed to a single result of a chosen duration — no case runs, no report is written, stdout and stderr are swallowed — so what is graded is the value `main()` RETURNS. One line short of the path CI takes: `evals/run.py`'s `if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())` tail is what turns that value into a process exit code, `_main_exit_code` calls `main()` in-process and never goes through it, and changing the tail to a bare `main()` would disable this ceiling — and the invariant and regression rules with it — with this case still green (PR #20 R13, Debt T-R13). The suite-key check is a set comparison rather than a row per suite name: rows can only ever cover the suites someone thought to list, and `full` was the one missing when `WALL_BUDGET_S["full"] = 1` was shown to slip through green (PR #20 R11). The env-override rows are all fallback except two, for the same reason: the dangerous direction is an override that quietly switches the gate off, not one that fails to apply. The env override is scoped to `fast` in `wall_budget` as of ADR-017: one env var cannot carry two suites' numbers, and on CI the fast override is 80 — five times what invariant costs, which would have reopened the valve there while closing it locally.
triage.not_covered: it grades total wall clock only — a case that gets 10s slower while another gets 10s faster is invisible to it; per-case timings are in every committed report for anyone looking. It does not drive `evals/run.py` as a process, so the module tail described above is ungraded. It does not exercise the `--update-baseline` path, which returns before the ceiling is consulted and reports nothing about it (PR #20 R12, Debt T-R12). Slower hardware is answered rather than uncovered: `EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S` gives an environment its own measured ceiling, and this case grades the override's fallbacks and the value the workflow declares — but nothing here checks that a declared number was ever measured. This case cannot tell a measured 75 from an invented one; only an ADR-013 amendment with runs behind it can.
triage.watched_red_adr017: both new assertions were watched red against the mutation each rules out. Removing the `if suite != 'fast': return base` scoping from `wall_budget`: wrong [{env: '80', suite: 'invariant', expected_ceiling: 15, got: 80.0}] — the CI override raising invariant's ceiling to five times what that suite costs. Removing `invariant` from WALL_BUDGET_S entirely: wrong [{suite: 'invariant', wall_seconds: 15.01, over: true}, {suite: 'invariant', wall_seconds: 999.0, over: true}, {env: '80', suite: 'invariant', expected_ceiling: 15, got: None}, {env: None, ...}, {ruling: 'suites', ...}] — the unbounded-relief-valve state this PR shipped one round ago.
